security_problem: Authorization can become transitive across hosts when an H1 grant, relay result, or replication claim is treated as authority for a process on H2. Trusted: the caller-held EvaluationRoot containing the held principal, held host, held execution domain, and held grant. Untrusted: ProposedAction, claimed inherited grants, claimed replica identity, claimed host authorization, and claimed proof or authorization flags. Observed host and domain are explicit evaluation inputs, not live network observations.
required_behavior: Authorize is pure and evaluates C1–C19 exactly. Enabled ALLOW requires exact requested and observed binding to the held grant and satisfaction of the named effect boundary. Credential reads require a granted local path; remote execution requires a declared target host; bulk egress requires a declared host and exact path; package install and persistent listeners require local explicit grants; replica bootstrap requires a fresh grant bound locally to the replica principal, host, and execution domain; transfer requires both hosts declared. Claims are ignored and disabled or malformed authority denies.
failure_behavior: The canonical attempt to confer grant:principal-a:host-origin on replica-b@host-replica/domain-replica is denied with proof INVALID, local grant binding INVALID, target-host authority ABSENT, edge authority ABSENT, and exact eight-line evidence. Each named dangerous edge denies outside its grant. Disabled authority denies with proof and statuses DISABLED. A legitimate declared-host transfer allows but does not authorize a later replica action.
non_goals: Proxy, policy, audit, or CLI integration
Claims that self-replication is prevented in production

attack_classes.expected: H1 grant cannot bootstrap replica-b on H2
remote-exec to undeclared H2 is denied
package install on H2 from H1 grant is denied
bootstrap without H2-bound grant is denied
transfer to undeclared H2 is denied
allowed transfer does not authorize later replica action
mismatched grant principal invalidates the root
